name: What is the difference between a junior ADU and a standard ADU?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a junior ADU and a standard ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU) is a smaller, interior ADU typically created within the existing footprint of a single-family home. JADUs are generally limited to 500 square feet and must include an efficiency kitchen, but they may share a bathroom with the main house or have a separate entrance. Standard ADUs are separate, self-contained living units that can be attached, detached, or converted from existing space. They typically have a full kitchen and bathroom and are often larger, offering more independence and flexibility.
acceptedAnswer.description: JADUs are smaller, interior units within a home, usually under 500 sq ft, with an efficiency kitchen. Standard ADUs are larger, self-contained units with full facilities.
